result.summary:
PASS. Independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs test/letflow/identity/tenant_test.exs test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs`: 74 passed, 0 failed. No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in any of the four files (grep confirmed). Each fixture (TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 with a unique slug_prefix per test) is self-generated per test, no shared hardcoded state, and tests read only their own setup's rows -- self-sufficient, no ordering dependency observed or plausible.

AC-by-AC: AC1 (tenants_test.exs:73-92) -- full Jason.decode!/1 equality against the exact 5-key problem-document literal (type/title/status/detail/trace_id), plus three redundant substring refutations (other tenant's slug, 'items', 'count') exactly as the design specifies; a regression that leaked a partial shape would fail the equality assertion even before the refutations run. AC2 (tenants_test.exs:105-160) -- four separate tests, one per verb (GET/PATCH/deactivate/reactivate), each snapshots tenant_b's row via Repo.get! before the cross-tenant call and re-asserts equality (or, for reactivate, the specific :status field) after; genuinely re-fetches rather than re-checking only the status code. AC3 (tenants_test.exs:166-205) -- read directly: both tests target admin_tenant.tenant.slug / own_tenant.tenant.slug, i.e. the SAME tenant as the caller's own auth_context.tenant_id in both the allow (PLATFORM_ADMIN) and deny (PROCESS_DESIGNER) cases -- this genuinely proves the own-tenant carve-out does not exist, not accidentally testing against a stranger's tenant. AC4 (tenants_test.exs:350-397) -- queries information_schema.tables directly for the 'events' table inside the real provisioned schema, not trusting the 201; :auto sandbox mode set first, matching the design's stated reason. AC6/AC7 -- doc-only, already REVIEWER-confirmed at Step 2d against the literal shipped @moduledoc text; re-spot-checked, still present verbatim.

AC5 -- read tenant_status_test.exs's 'REQ-075 AC5' describe blocks (lines ~215-260) directly. Dispatch is NOT via Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline as the design's illustrative test sketch showed, nor is it a bare Letflow.Routers.Tenants sub-router call (which was the design's actual concern -- that path would never invoke TenantStatus and would pass vacuously). Instead these tests call Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus.call/2 directly with a constructed conn.assigns.auth_context, which is the SAME plug function the full ApiPipeline chain invokes -- this is a legitimate, non-vacuous equivalent: it exercises the actual :inactive-check logic directly rather than through an unnecessary full-pipeline detour, and matches this same test file's own already-established pattern for the pre-existing :migrating check. Judgment: satisfies AC5 and the 'or equivalent' clause of the gate; not a gap.

Mutation test (gate point 8): ran one myself rather than relying on the two prior structural reads. In a clean worktree (git status --porcelain lib/ test/ empty beforehand), inverted lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex's with_authorization/4 case branches (:Deny403 -> call fun.(conn); allow -> Response.forbidden/2), i.e. exactly backwards. Ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs`: Result: 0/20 passed, Failed: 20 tests -- every single test in the file caught the inversion. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/ test/`; confirmed via `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` (empty) and a fresh `mix test test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs` re-run: Result: 20 passed. The suite genuinely discriminates a correct authorization ordering from an inverted one, not merely a suite that happens to pass either way.

No rework required. Ordering deviation (Step 3 merged into Step 2a) is noted per instruction but does not affect this gate's outcome -- the shipped tests meet the same bar this gate would apply to a separately-authored TEST-DESIGNER submission.
